units.function: Pure helper defining Tool Profile binding specificity, selecting only the narrowest matching scope and deterministically ordering/deduplicating Profile IDs.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends only on the shared target-type union; ToolAccessPolicyService feeds it all matching database bindings before loading Profiles and entries. It is policy infrastructure, not a domain authority.
units.keyDataModels: Profile binding with profileId, target type, priority and creation time; specificity order gateway, issue, routine, agent, project, company.
units.lifecycle: Find the minimum specificity rank among matching bindings, discard every broader binding, sort winners by priority/creation/profile ID and deduplicate Profile IDs while retaining first occurrence.
units.testAssessment: No dedicated test unit was found; issue-over-company and agent-over-project behavior is covered indirectly by the audited Tool Policy integration suite. Missing are every precedence pair, same-scope ties, duplicate Profile bindings, invalid dates, empty input, deterministic property tests and semantic conflicts between exclude/default-deny/allow entries across multiple winner Profiles. In the consumer, an exclude skips only that Profile; a later same-scope Profile may still allow, so 'exclude' is not a hard deny and the name can be misleading.
units.designRationale: Let the most context-specific Tool configuration replace broad defaults while producing stable evaluation order for multiple Profiles at the same scope.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs explicit, explainable composition rules across Company, department/position, project, Work, Agent, Connector and runtime Tool/Data policies without accidentally treating a local allow as stronger than a mandatory global deny.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the pure specificity ranking and deterministic ordering, but separate mandatory guardrails from overridable defaults. Define deny/allow composition algebra, provenance and conflict codes; generate exhaustive precedence tests and include Responsibility/Data/Approval scope layers. Return a compiled policy explanation rather than only Profile IDs.
units.responsibilityConflict: Specificity alone cannot decide authority: a narrow Issue/Profile allow may not override Company data-egress, legal, separation-of-duties or accountable-human requirements. The helper carries no owner, approver, effective version or evidence.

units.function: Database-backed per-Company/minute metric counter, currently specialized to recording Tool runtime audit-write failures with a best-effort wrapper.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends directly on Drizzle and the Tool runtime metric table. Tool Policy and execution services call it when durable audit writes fail; the fallback logs to process stderr.
units.keyDataModels: Company ID, arbitrary metric string, UTC minute bucket, atomic count and timestamps; audit_write_failed constant.
units.lifecycle: Insert count=1 for the current minute or atomically increment on the Company/metric/bucket conflict key. If that write fails, swallow the error after logging Company and error message.
units.testAssessment: No dedicated tests were found for bucketing, concurrent increments, tenant isolation, failure swallowing, time boundaries, retention/cardinality or the fallback path. The atomic SQL increment is sound for one database, but audit failure and metric failure share the same persistence dependency, so a database outage removes both evidence and the counter. Console output is not an independently durable alert channel.
units.designRationale: Avoid masking the original Tool operation with observability failures while retaining a cheap tenant-scoped signal when an audit write fails transiently.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must surface missing audit/evidence writes through an independent operational channel and may need fail-stop behavior for high-risk execution rather than best-effort continuation.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY. Keep atomic low-cardinality counters, but emit through an ObservabilityPort independent of the evidence store, alert on sustained failures and define risk-tier behavior: fail closed before high-risk execution when a DecisionReceipt cannot be durably committed; allow explicitly classified low-risk degradation only with a local tamper-evident spool.
units.responsibilityConflict: Swallowing an audit-write failure can leave an action without responsibility evidence. A best-effort counter in the same failing database does not restore the chain of custody or prove who authorized and executed the Tool action.
